summary: On the TCP transport with the durable authority ledger, the elected replayer's recovery-complete ladder (mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_complete2) calls mxfs_dlm_ledger_purge_owner for the dead node and IGNORES its return. A partial purge (-EIO at some page: the victim's holder bits on later pages remain on the platter) is followed by mxfs_dlm_purge_node (the table's imported blockers for the victim are dropped), the page takeover, the heartbeat-slot zero (the broadcast) and the slot's republication as EMPTY. That is the ordering the sess424 design ruling forbids: a slot republished while ledger bits of its previous occupant remain means the next occupant of the slot inherits durable holder bits it never acquired (a slot-indexed bitmap cannot tell the old holder from the new occupant), and every survivor that dropped the table blockers can now decide grants the ledger will refuse (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT) or, for a page whose blocker was never imported, over a bit that will surface as an unretirable ghost on the next import. Measured on the rig: two partial purges (rc=-5) on test20 during the 0.34.0 formation, completion proceeded.
mechanism: dlm/v5_mount.c mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_complete2 step 2 (sess422 step 3f): v5_refresh_active_nodes; mxfs_dlm_ledger_purge_owner(ctx->dlm, dead_node, dead_slot) — return value discarded; mxfs_dlm_purge_node; v5_handoff_takeover; then step 3 mxfs_disklock_purge_node (the broadcast) and step 4 publication. The CAW purge failure at the same site (P230-COMPLETE-PURGEFAIL) is a HELD failure (V5_COMPLETE_HELD_FAIL, ladder retries); the ledger purge is not. dlm/tauth_ledger.c mxfs_tauth_ledger_purge_owner logs P-TAUTH-PURGE-PARTIAL and returns the page's commit rc (-EIO proven-not-committed / -ENOTRECOVERABLE poisoned / -ESTALE not ours) with 'blockers beyond this page remain'. Ordering invariant (sess424 shape-A ruling, banked in the sess424 transcript and docs/history/end-state-and-next.md): a slot is republished only after every ledger record naming its previous occupant is retired.
